candidates.label: Kawasaki disease (incomplete)
missing_or_uncertain: Other Kawasaki criteria (oral changes, extremity changes, lymphadenopathy) not mentioned

candidates.label: Multisystem inflammatory syndrome in children (MIS-C)
missing_or_uncertain: Recent COVID-19 exposure or antibody testing not documented

candidates.label: Viral infection (e.g., adenovirus) with conjunctivitis and exanthem
missing_or_uncertain: Viral PCR or serology not performed

candidates.label: Drug-induced hypersensitivity syndrome (DIHS) / DRESS
missing_or_uncertain: Eosinophilia or organ involvement not mentioned

response.rationale: The combination of prolonged fever, bilateral nonpurulent conjunctivitis, erythema multiforme-type rash, and markedly elevated inflammatory markers in a child unresponsive to antibiotics strongly suggests Kawasaki disease. Negative blood cultures and PCR reduce likelihood of bacterial or acute COVID-19. Other systemic inflammatory conditions are less consistent with the specific rash and conjunctivitis.
